flashcards.back: Distance travelled per unit time, calculated as distance divided by time, measured in metres per second.
Speed with a direction: displacement divided by time, so a round trip back to the start has zero average velocity.
The straight-line change in position from start to finish, with a direction - not the total path length.
The rate of change of velocity, read off a velocity-time graph as its gradient.
Rise over run on a graph: on a distance-time graph it is the speed, and on a velocity-time graph it is the acceleration.
The product of velocity and time accumulated under the line, which equals the distance travelled.

Flat reads as "nothing is happening", so the line feels like zero movement. A flat v-t line means constant velocity: the object keeps moving at the same speed. In class, sketch a line flat at 10 m/s and ask how far the object travels in 5 seconds: the area under the flat line is 10 times 5, which is 50 metres - a stopped object travels nowhere.
flashcards.front: A flat line on a velocity-time graph means the object has stopped.

flashcards.back: Wrong - the velocity stays constant at 12 m/s, so the object keeps moving
